title: A Machine Learning-Based Model for Predicting High Deficiency Risk Ships in Port State Control: A Case Study of the Port of Singapore
content:
Port State Control (PSC) is a vital mechanism for ensuring maritime safety and environ-mental protection. However, limited inspection resources and the growing number of vessels pose significant challenges in efficiently identifying high-risk ships. This study leverages machine learning techniques to develop a predictive model capable of identify-ing vessels with a high likelihood of deficiencies, using PSC inspection data from the Port of Singapore between 2014 and 2022. A total of 10,736 inspection records encompassing 16 relevant features were analyzed. Inspections with five or more recorded deficiencies were classified as high-risk cases.
Following comprehensive data preprocessing and feature engineering, a Random Forest classifier was developed and benchmarked against baseline Decision Tree and XGBoost models. The Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of 81.8%, a precision of 80.5%, and a recall of 83.0%, significantly outperforming the baseline model. Key predictors iden-tified include vessel age, gross tonnage, company performance, and flag state—factors that align closely with international maritime safety standards.
The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of applying data-driven methods to enhance PSC operations. Beyond regulatory applications, this approach also enables shipping companies to proactively identify and address potential deficiencies. The study provides a robust empirical foundation for implementing intelligent risk alert systems in port inspections and contributes to the broader goal of advancing global maritime safety and regulatory efficiency.
